subject: Persistent data ownership and handoff for EU ↔ APAC private deployments
messages:

Subject: Persistent data ownership and handoff for EU ↔ APAC private deployments

Hi all,

Quick kickoff on the Seaworthy private-deploy review: they want a clear operational and contractual picture for "persistent data ownership" when we run private deployments in both EU and APAC regions. Key asks from legal/commercial: who holds the canonical copy, what triggers cross-region replication (if any), KMS ownership, and an auditable handoff process during an emergency failover.

Attached is a short checklist I drafted to structure the conversation (persistent-data-handoff-checklist.pdf). High-level questions to answer before Friday:
- Primary custody model: single-region canonical or dual-write?
- KMS: customer-managed keys (bring-your-own) or Redwood-managed with split custody?
- Backup and retention: where snapshots live and who can request exports
- Failover trigger matrix: who authorizes failover, how we record it, and evidence retention

Soojin / Lauren — can you review the checklist and add operational notes (network cutover steps, peering/egress constraints)? Jonas — can you sketch the routing/peering requirements for an APAC standby that remains within customer control (if needed)?

Hiro / Acme — would be helpful if you can confirm what Seaworthy expects legally (contractual custody vs operational custody) and any local regulator constraints in JP/EU that we should bake into the failover authorization flow.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Persistent data ownership and handoff for EU ↔ APAC private deployments

Marcus — thanks for the checklist, that helps. A few quick clarifying questions from Seaworthy and our compliance team:

1) Evidence: they want a small, auditable artifact for every failover event (timestamped decision, who authorized, pre/post checksum of the active dataset). Is that something Redwood can emit automatically?
2) KMS: Seaworthy prefers customer-managed keys in EU; they may accept Redwood-managed in APAC under certain contractual guarantees. We need a clear KMS ownership matrix per-region.
3) Replication model: they are allergic to dual-write due to consistency concerns. Preferred approach is region-primary with cross-region read-replica that is logically isolated until an authorized failover.

I attached a short list of regulatory constraints from Seaworthy's legal (they redacted internal notes) — see kms-ownership-matrix.xlsx.

We'll plan a call tomorrow 10:00 UTC to walk through.

— Acme Cloud Security (on behalf of Seaworthy)

Subject: Re: Persistent data ownership and handoff for EU ↔ APAC private deployments

Thanks — quick operational notes after reading the checklist and Seaworthy constraints:

- Canonical copy: implement single-region canonical (EU primary for EU customers) with an async read-replica in APAC that is encrypted at rest and kept logically quarantined (no automatic promotion). Promotion requires a signed, auditable action with two authorizers (operator + customer security lead).

- KMS: support BYOK (customer-provided CMK) in EU. For APAC standby we can offer Redwood-managed keys but must record key usage logs and provide KMS audit export on request.

- Network / cutover steps (high-level):
  * Pre-cutover: validate replication lag < 15s, take snapshot markers, capture dataset checksums, freeze writes to primary
  * Authorization: receive signed failover request (DocuSign or similarly auditable), then flip routing via BGP/DNS and promote replica
  * Post-cutover: run data integrity check, rotate ephemeral access tokens, and start asynchronous re-replication to a new standby in the original primary region (if required)

- Evidence capture: we can auto-generate an event bundle (JSON) containing timestamps, operator IDs, checksums, and the DocuSign reference. Need product to wire that into retention policy (30/90/365 days per contract).

I sketched a minimal sketch (eu-apac-network-sketch.png) with required load balancer and peering lanes — attaching.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-03T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Persistent data ownership and handoff for EU ↔ APAC private deployments

Adding some routing/ops specifics to Soojin's proposal:

- Routing: prefer BGP session peering between customer edge and Redwood transit in each region. For cutover, we will prep a pre-signed route-filter change and a DNS TTL plan (60s pre-cutover, then 30s during).

- Egress & peering: to keep the APAC standby within customer control we will peer directly into their VPC using private VRF. No public egress required for dataset replication — use mutual TLS over the private link.

- Promotion automation: we can automate pre-checks (replication lag, checksum pass) but require manual gating for the signed approval. Post-promotion, an automated rollback window (10 minutes) is supported if integrity checks fail.

- Operational runbook link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example_shared/Seaworthy-handoff (working doc — will add detailed BGP snippets).

— Jonas

Subject: Re: Persistent data ownership and handoff for EU ↔ APAC private deployments — decision log and owners

Team — good discussion. Summarizing decisions and owners so we have an auditable start:

Decisions:
- Canonical copy model: EU-primary, APAC standby replica (async, quarantined). No dual-write (agreed).
- KMS: BYOK mandatory in EU; Redwood-managed optional in APAC with audit export guarantees.
- Failover authorization: two-authorizer model (operator + customer security lead) via DocuSign; auto-generated event bundle stored for 365 days by default unless customer contracts a different retention.
- Promotion: manual gate with automated pre-checks and 10-minute rollback window.

Owners / next actions (due dates):
- Soojin: produce runbook with explicit snapshot/checksum commands and retention hook (due 2026-12-10) — attachment: eu-apac-runbook-draft
- Jonas: add BGP snippets and pre-signed route filter template to runbook + test plan (due 2026-12-12) — link to runbook in Drive
- Naomi (Legal): draft contract language for KMS ownership and failover authorization (due 2026-12-09)
- Marcus: coordinate Seaworthy signoff meeting (target 2026-12-08)

Acme / Seaworthy — please confirm that the above model meets your minimum regulatory constraints. If yes, Naomi will circulate proposed contract language and we'll schedule the cutover tabletop exercise after signoff.

Thanks all,
Marcus
